lines.display: We eat *raw* *salmon* and *tuna* all the time,
lines.spoken: We eat raw salmon and tuna all the time,
but serving raw eel is strictly off limits.

lines.display: That's because eel *blood* hides a dangerous *protein* *toxin*
lines.spoken: That's because eel blood hides a dangerous protein toxin
called ichthyo-hemotoxin.

lines.display: Imagine a *single* *drop* of fresh eel blood
lines.spoken: Imagine a single drop of fresh eel blood

lines.display: splashing into a *tiny* *cut* on a chef's hand.
lines.spoken: splashing into a tiny cut on a chef's hand.
If we zoom inside that liquid,
we find jagged, spiked protein molecules suspended in the serum.

lines.display: Unlike typical poisons that only hurt you if *swallowed,*
lines.spoken: Unlike typical poisons that only hurt you if swallowed,
this protein attacks on immediate surface contact.

lines.display: The second it touches an *open* *wound* or *mucous* *membrane,*
lines.spoken: The second it touches an open wound or mucous membrane,

lines.display: it rapidly *binds* to the tissue, triggering extreme *burning* and *swelling.*
lines.spoken: it rapidly binds to the tissue, triggering extreme burning and swelling.

lines.display: But this biological weapon has one major weakness:
lines.spoken: But this biological weapon has one major weakness:
Heat.
At just sixty degrees for five minutes,
the toxic protein completely unravels and breaks apart.

lines.display: So if one raw drop causes that much *pain,*
lines.spoken: So if one raw drop causes that much pain,
the whole fish is a passive hazard.

lines.display: But putting that fillet over a *hot* *grill*
lines.spoken: But putting that fillet over a hot grill
permanently destroys every trace of the toxin,
making it completely safe to eat.
